replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: I think you’re talking about the Tanfield Valley/Nanook site on Baffin Island. That one is fascinating, archaeologists have found possible Norse-linked evidence there, including metalworking traces, whetstones and unusual stone construction. But the yarn/cordage part is more complicated than it first appeared: later dating showed Dorset people were making spun yarn centuries before Norse contact, so that evidence by itself doesn’t prove an earlier Viking settlement. L’Anse aux Meadows is still the only confirmed Norse site in the Americas, with secure activity dated to AD 1021.
